description:
What usually goes wrong for these goods on this lane, and what to check
before committing: sourced practitioner notes.

`hs6_codes` (six-digit codes) and `corridor_id` are optional; without them
only notes for any goods or lane come back. `lane_covered` and
`chapter_specific` say whether anything more specific matched; if no note is
written for the lane, `lane_note` says so. `direction`: `buy` (goods come
home) or `sell` (goods go to the lane's other end); a line for goods
entering the other country is left out; omitted, both are served. A lane
without the UK gets no UK-only line. `proposed` and `rejected` count lines
a model proposed and lines refused for promising a fixed timeframe.

Each line carries its citation: `source_url`, `source_title`, `reviewed` (the date a person checked it against that source), `synthesis` (a reading of several sources rather than one source's words) and `pdf`. A line with no source is not served, so `every_line_sourced` is true. Information, not advice.
